candidates.decision_relevance: Timestamped hourly BTC, ETH, ETH/BTC, funding, open interest, aggressive flow, depth/taker imbalance, CFGI, liquidations and price/VWAP observations would resolve the repeated sequence-order and cross-horizon uncertainty around transient pullbacks versus persistent deterioration or re-acceleration.
candidates.evidence_reference: W33-W35 reviews; daily outputs from 2026-09-02 through 2026-09-06
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied records contain mostly endpoint comparisons, unavailable or zero-span short horizons, and inconsistent actual spans, preventing reconstruction of whether price weakness, leverage change, flow deterioration and sentiment shifts preceded one another.

candidates.decision_relevance: A membership-stable, timestamped breadth history split by large-cap and broader universes would materially test whether reported participation deterioration or recovery was persistent rather than an artifact of changing top-100 proxy membership.
candidates.evidence_reference: All daily outputs and W33-W35 reviews
candidates.metric_name: Canonical-compatible breadth path with membership snapshots
candidates.missing_history_problem: Breadth is repeatedly described as a point-in-time top-100 proxy with changing membership hashes; the records cannot establish durable participation expansion, narrowing or transmission.

candidates.decision_relevance: Complete, timestamped liquidation and positioning events with venue coverage, long/short attribution and price response would distinguish healthy deleveraging from forced selling and test whether leverage stress preceded subsequent weakness or recovery.
candidates.metric_name: Complete liquidation and positioning event history
candidates.missing_history_problem: Liquidations are lower-bound aggregates from a fragile source with unknown truncation, while open-interest changes are directionally ambiguous and lack comparable historical event context.

candidates.decision_relevance: A consecutive settled BTC and ETH ETF flow history, including within-week sequencing and concentration, would test whether positive demand persisted and translated into price support during breadth or leadership weakness.
candidates.evidence_reference: W35 review and daily outputs dated 2026-09-03 through 2026-09-06
candidates.metric_name: Settled ETF net-flow sequence by asset and fund
candidates.missing_history_problem: Only isolated settled sessions are supplied; weekly totals cannot be assessed for persistence, concentration, sequencing or offsetting flows.

candidates.decision_relevance: A timestamp-aligned macro history would provide missing cross-asset context for distinguishing crypto-specific deleveraging and rotation failure from broader liquidity or risk-appetite shocks.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Macro owner data are repeatedly absent or disabled, so the analyses cannot evaluate whether observed crypto weakness coincided with a broader macro impulse.

candidates.decision_relevance: Historical stablecoin supply, exchange balances and transfer/deployment observations would test whether supply growth represented usable market liquidity or merely passive issuance.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Only isolated supply changes are reported, explicitly without evidence of deployment or risk-appetite transmission.

candidates.decision_relevance: Archived forecast definitions, issue times, evidence cutoffs, horizons, ranges, confidence fields and matured outcomes would permit ex-ante audit, precision assessment, calibration and measurement of false-positive, false-negative and opportunity-cost behavior.
candidates.evidence_reference: W33-W35 reviews; all daily forecast candidate sections
candidates.missing_history_problem: The reviews repeatedly state that candidates, cutoffs and matured outcomes are absent or zero, preventing verification of hindsight leakage, broad-range containment, forecast skill and warning calibration.
